legend: Every flag below is attached to at least one row and is shown on the Flagged for Review page. A flag is not proof of wrongdoing — it marks something a buyer cannot confirm from the seller's own page and must resolve before paying.

flags.label: Weight not published
flags.what: The seller's page does not state the ring's metal weight in grams, so melt value cannot be computed and the price-per-gram test cannot be applied.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires the weight before purchase. Without it, any price-per-gram figure would be an invention.
flags.action: Ask the seller in writing for the weight in grams (and whether it is gold-only or total item weight). Keep the reply.

flags.label: Hallmark and/or maker's mark not published
flags.what: The page does not describe the stamp inside the band or the manufacturer's mark.
flags.why_it_matters: National Stamping Act (15 U.S.C. 297), summarised in 16 CFR 23.10, requires a quality mark on gold to be accompanied by the maker's trademark or name. A karat stamp with no maker's mark is incomplete.
flags.action: Ask for a close-up photo of the stamp before purchase; verify both the karat and the maker's mark.

flags.label: "18k" in the name, but not solid gold
flags.what: The piece is 18k gold vermeil: a gold layer over a sterling silver base. The seller's own spec says the 18k gold is a plating layer on recycled sterling silver.
flags.why_it_matters: 16 CFR 23.4 defines vermeil as a sterling silver base plated with gold of a stated thickness. A buyer scanning for "18k" could reasonably assume solid gold.
flags.action: Do not treat this as a solid-gold ring. If solid gold is required, exclude it.

flags.label: "Solid" is not stated by the seller
flags.what: The seller states the karat (e.g. 14K / 18K) but never uses the word "solid".
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires the listing to say solid gold explicitly. A karat alone does not rule out hollow construction, plating over base metal, or a two-metal build.
flags.action: Get written confirmation that the item is solid 14k/18k gold throughout, and that it is not hollow.

flags.label: Price is the setting only
flags.what: The figure shown is Blue Nile's "Setting Price". The centre diamond is priced separately, so the delivered ring costs more than the number in this table.
flags.why_it_matters: Comparing a setting price against a complete ring's price is an apples-to-oranges comparison. Any price-per-gram or melt test done on the setting price alone is meaningless.
flags.action: Add a centre stone to the builder and record the all-in total before comparing.

flags.label: Price not displayed on the page
flags.what: The product page as fetched showed no price for this item.
flags.why_it_matters: No price means no comparison is possible, and no price was invented to fill the gap.
flags.action: Check the price while signed in, or at a warehouse, and record it with the date and a screenshot.

flags.label: Return policy excludes precious metals
flags.what: Costco's official return policy lists "Precious metals are non-refundable".
flags.why_it_matters: This conflicts directly with your requirement that you can return the ring after inspecting it. Gold jewellery is a precious metal.
flags.action: Confirm in writing, for this specific item, whether a return is possible before buying. If not, this deal fails your checklist.

flags.label: Very short return window
flags.what: Wilson's requires contact within 7 calendar days of delivery, then the item must be shipped back within 3 calendar days of receiving the return label. Items are sold "as is". Cancelled orders are not refunded the 3% card processing fee.
flags.why_it_matters: An independent jeweller's assay or XRF test usually needs an appointment. A 7-day window can expire before verification is possible — the exact failure mode your checklist warns about.
flags.action: Line up the appraiser before delivery, or negotiate the return window in writing.

flags.label: Bank wire accepted as a payment method
flags.what: Blue Nile's return policy refers to refunds being issued back via bank wire or ACH, which means bank wire is an accepted way to pay.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist prefers a credit card for purchase protection and warns against irreversible payment methods. A wire is money you cannot claw back through a chargeback.
flags.action: Pay by credit card even if a wire discount is offered.

flags.label: Engraving voids the return
flags.what: Mejuri and Blue Nile both exclude engraved or personalised items from returns. Mejuri adds that free engraving is optional but makes the item non-returnable.
flags.why_it_matters: A free engraving can quietly convert a returnable ring into a final sale — exactly the exclusion your checklist tells you to look for.
flags.action: Skip engraving until after the ring has been inspected and verified.

flags.label: Large-diamond return is a credit memo, not a refund
flags.what: For diamonds of 1.00 ct or larger, Costco requires all original IGI/GIA paperwork and issues a jewellery credit memo after its own gemologist inspects the stone.
flags.why_it_matters: A credit memo is store credit, not money back. It also assumes you kept the certificate — so documentation retention is part of your return path.
flags.action: Keep every certificate and appraisal with the receipt from day one.

flags.label: Weight includes the stones
flags.what: The published weight is "total weight" of the finished ring, diamonds included. Gold-only weight is lower, so a melt calculation using this number is an upper bound, not the gold content.
flags.why_it_matters: Using total item weight as gold weight systematically overstates melt value — a classic way an otherwise honest calculator produces a wrong number.
flags.action: Ask for the mounting weight excluding stones, or accept that the melt figure is a ceiling.

flags.label: No independent assay or XRF result
flags.what: No seller in this study publishes a per-item XRF scan or an independent assay. The karat is the seller's own statement, backed at most by a stamp.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist's key point: a stamp proves nothing by itself. Every row here still needs post-delivery verification by an independent jeweller.
flags.action: Commission XRF or assay on arrival, before wearing or resizing.

flags.label: Unusual karat / not gold throughout
flags.what: This piece is stamped 19 karat — uncommon in the US market — and carries black enamel inlay, so part of the item is not gold.
flags.why_it_matters: 19K is 79.17% gold by definition, but an unusual fineness deserves an assay rather than trust. Enamel also means the item is not gold throughout.
flags.action: Have the fineness assayed; treat the enamel areas as non-gold in any value estimate.

flags.label: Product page not individually fetched
flags.what: The row's price comes from Blue Nile's official engagement-ring listing, which displays "Setting Price" next to each item.
flags.why_it_matters: The listing is an official source, but an individual item page is stronger evidence and may carry extra exclusions.
flags.action: Open the item page and re-confirm price, metal and exclusions before buying.

flags.label: Independent review research not completed
flags.what: Independent third-party reviews/complaints were not verified against a primary review source in this session, so no reputation score is asserted.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires independent review research. Inventing a rating would be a hallucination, so this is left open.
flags.action: Check BBB, Trustpilot and state AG complaint databases before buying.

flags.label: Product page says the item is non-returnable
flags.what: Tiffany & Co.'s own product page for The Tiffany Setting states: "Please note that this item is non returnable" and "this item can only be exchanged".
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires that you can return the ring after inspecting it, including after an independent test. Exchange-only means you cannot get your money back if the assay disappoints.
flags.action: Get the return terms confirmed in writing for the exact configuration before paying. If exchange-only stands, the ring fails your return requirement.

flags.label: Rhodium-plated surface on white gold
flags.what: The listing states a rhodium finish on 14K white gold.
flags.why_it_matters: Rhodium is a surface plating over the gold alloy, not the body metal. 16 CFR 23.7 requires that this surface layer be disclosed, and it wears away with time.
flags.action: Budget for re-plating every few years, or choose yellow gold if you do not want a plated surface.

flags.label: Weight is explicitly approximate
flags.what: The seller publishes a gram weight but qualifies it: "All weights and measurements are approximate".
flags.why_it_matters: An approximate weight still beats no weight, but melt-value maths on it inherits that uncertainty.
flags.action: Treat the melt figure as indicative; ask for the actual weight of the specific piece before shipping.

flags.label: Very light band
flags.what: A published weight under 1 gram for a full ring.
flags.why_it_matters: At this weight there is very little gold, so the melt value is small relative to the asking price, and the band will feel and wear differently from a heavier ring. It is the clearest illustration of why the gram figure matters more than the karat badge.
flags.action: Decide whether you want a ring this light before comparing it on price alone.

flags.label: Two metals in one ring
flags.what: An 18k yellow gold band combined with a platinum head.
flags.why_it_matters: 16 CFR 23.8 requires the relative quantities of precious metals in a multi-metal product to be disclosed and listed in order of weight. "18k gold" alone does not describe this ring's composition.
flags.action: Ask which metal dominates by weight before valuing the gold content.

flags.label: "Starting from" price
flags.what: The price shown is the entry configuration, not a fixed price for the ring pictured.
flags.why_it_matters: The figure varies with the centre stone. Comparing it with a fixed price elsewhere compares two different things.
flags.action: Configure the exact stone you want and record that total, with the date.

flags.label: Availability unclear or unavailable
flags.what: The page showed unavailable or sold-out indicators during verification.
flags.why_it_matters: A price you cannot actually transact at is not a live price.
flags.action: Confirm stock before relying on the price.

flags.label: Listing is dead or redirects
flags.what: The product URL now 404s, is sold out, or redirects to a different retailer.
flags.why_it_matters: Dead listings are excluded from the price table rather than quoted from a stale copy.
flags.action: None — recorded for completeness.

flags.label: Return policy page not read
flags.what: James Allen's returns were checked twice and its policy page has still not been read, so its return terms remain unknown rather than favourable. This flag was also carried by Ross-Simons and Catbird rows; both policies were read on the official sites (2026-10-22 and again 2026-10-23) and the flag was removed from those rows.
flags.why_it_matters: An unread policy is not a permissive one. Assuming a return right that has not been verified is how buyers get stuck.
flags.action: Read the seller's return policy before ordering and keep a copy.
flags.correction_note: Re-scoped 2026-10-23 by arena/699d8e05-gold3: Ross-Simons' 30-Day No-Risk Returns Guarantee was read at https://www.ross-simons.com/pages/returns-exchanges and Catbird's 20-day window at https://www.catbirdnyc.com/returns on 2026-10-22/23. POL1 now applies to James Allen only. Published as finding F17.

flags.label: Seller page contradicts itself on metal/karat
flags.what: The listing title and spec table say 18K White Gold, while the same page's product description says the ring is "crafted from warmly lustrous 14k yellow gold".
flags.why_it_matters: If the seller's own page cannot agree with itself about the metal, the karat stamp is the only thing left to trust — and that is exactly what your checklist says not to rely on alone.
flags.action: Ask the seller in writing which alloy the ring is made in and get the answer on the product page or by email. Have the metal tested (XRF) on arrival before accepting it.

flags.label: Product URL redirects to a different product path
flags.what: The linked Tiffany URL redirects to a different product path (/jewelry/rings/18k-rose-gold-and-platinum-diamond-rings-1712.html). The page served there still shows The Tiffany Setting in 18k yellow gold, so the facts were verified, but the link is not stable.
flags.why_it_matters: A redirect can silently land a buyer on a different product later. A dead or drifting link is how a stale price becomes an invented one.
flags.action: Re-open the link before buying and confirm the title, price and metal on the page you land on.

flags.label: Identifier on the page differs from the identifier in the URL
flags.what: The Costco URL ends in /100675127, while the page that loads shows "Item 1596365". The product title matched, so the row is kept, but the two identifiers disagree.
flags.why_it_matters: If you quote an item number to Costco or to a card issuer in a dispute, the wrong one can void your complaint trail.
flags.action: Use the item number printed on the page (1596365) and keep a dated screenshot of it next to the URL.

flags.label: Published weight is explicitly approximate
flags.what: The seller publishes a gram weight but qualifies it. Sarraf states an accuracy of ± 5%; Ross-Simons states that all weights and measurements are approximate.
flags.why_it_matters: A tolerance turns a precise-looking melt calculation into a range. Presenting the midpoint as fact would overstate the precision of the number.
flags.action: Treat any melt figure from this weight as an estimate within the seller's stated tolerance, and confirm the actual weight on a jeweller's scale after delivery.

flags.label: Weight published for a reference size, not the size you order
flags.what: Sarraf states: "The weight listed is an approximate weight of a ring in size 10". The ring is sold in sizes 3 to 16.
flags.why_it_matters: Metal weight changes with ring size. Using the size-10 figure for a size 5 ring overstates its gold content.
flags.action: Ask for the weight of the exact size you intend to buy, or weigh the delivered ring before arguing about value.

flags.label: One weight covers more than one metal option
flags.what: Automic Gold states "Approximately 5.4g for gold or 8.1g for platinum" — one line covering two metals with different densities.
flags.why_it_matters: If you order the platinum version, the gold figure is the wrong number, and vice versa. A single value read out of context becomes a false claim.
flags.action: Quote the metal alongside the weight whenever you rely on it, and check the delivered ring's weight.

flags.label: Return window exists but is conditional and short-fused
flags.what: Sarraf accepts returns within 30 days of receipt, but the window is heavily conditional: items that are damaged or used do not qualify, orders past 30 days from receipt are refused, items from which the Sarraf.com tag has been removed are not eligible, and anything resized by a jeweller other than Sarraf Jewelry Inc., altered, special-ordered or damaged cannot be accepted for return. The seller's own policy pages charge no card-processing fee on a return; the only fees named are a non-refundable $25.00 engraving fee and $50.00 finish charge.
flags.why_it_matters: A return right you cannot practically use is not protection. Waiting past the window, or wearing the ring once, can end it.
flags.action: Inspect on arrival, keep the packaging untouched, and start the return in writing inside the window if anything fails verification.
flags.correction_note: Corrected 2026-10-23 by arena/699d8e05-gold3 (third re-verification pass). This entry previously read 'A cancelled order is charged a 3% card-processing fee (Wilson's terms state the same fee structure)'. That is not a Sarraf term. The 3% cancellation fee is Wilson's Estate Jewelry's own wording (recorded at RET2 / S-WE, verified verbatim on two Wilson's product pages on 2026-10-22). Sarraf's returns policy was read end to end on 2026-10-22 and again on 2026-10-23 at https://www.sarraf.com/30-day-returns-and-exchange-policy/ (2 chunks) and on the product-page 'Return Policy' tab; neither mentions any percentage fee. Published as finding F15.

flags.label: Engraving makes the item final sale
flags.what: The product page states that engraved items are final sale, and engraving is offered as an option at checkout.
flags.why_it_matters: A free or cheap engraving can quietly remove the return right that the rest of the policy advertises.
flags.action: Decline engraving until the ring has been independently verified, or accept that the purchase becomes non-returnable.

flags.label: $300 recycling fee on engagement-ring refunds (and store-credit-only over $15,000)
flags.what: VRAI's live Help Center return article states that ALL engagement ring returns (<$15,000) refunded to the original payment method incur a $300 recycling fee ($50 on wedding bands and made-to-order jewelry), waived only when taking VRAI gift-card store credit, and items above $15,000 receive store credit ONLY. Its Los Angeles BBB profile also carries an unaccredited F rating.
flags.why_it_matters: A mandatory $300 deduction penalises any buyer who exercises a cash refund after independent inspection, and orders above $15,000 forfeit cash refund rights altogether.
flags.action: Do not engrave or resize before independent scale and XRF verification, factor the $300 fee into your risk budget, and pay by credit card.

flags.label: 14-day original-payment cutoff inside 90-day credit window
flags.what: Local Eclectic advertises a 90-day return window, but its official FAQ restricts refunds to the original payment method to 14 days from delivery (days 15-90 receive store credit only, minus return label cost).
flags.why_it_matters: Store credit traps your funds with the same seller if independent XRF testing reveals an alloy discrepancy on day 15.
flags.action: Complete independent jeweller weighing and XRF testing within 10 days of delivery so any return falls inside the 14-day cash refund cutoff.

flags.label: 7-day return window and 10% restocking fee on cash refunds
flags.what: Menē limits returns to 7 days from receipt; full value is issued only as Menē Credit, whereas a refund to the original payment method deducts a 10% restocking fee (support.mene.com policy 4407022465633).
flags.why_it_matters: A 7-day window plus a 10% cash-refund restocking fee leaves minimal time and high cost if you need to return after independent inspection.
flags.action: Book your independent XRF appointment before delivery, keep the Certificate of Authenticity intact, and pay by credit card.

flags.label: 9k vs 10k karat contradiction on product page
flags.what: Local Eclectic's Solid Gold Simple Knot Ring page displays a '9k Solid Gold' material badge (37.5% Au, below the US 10K karat-gold threshold in 16 CFR 23.3) while the Product Materials bullet states '10k solid yellow gold'.
flags.why_it_matters: Under 16 CFR 23.3(b), an item below 10 karat cannot be marketed simply as karat gold in the US, and conflicting specs make true fineness uncertain online.
flags.action: Do not purchase without written confirmation of >=10K fineness and post-arrival XRF verification.

flags.label: Resizing badge contradicts product details exclusion
flags.what: Brilliant Earth's Fairmined 2mm Six-Prong Solitaire page displays a 'Free 1-Year Resizing' badge while its Product Details section states 'resizing is not available for this ring'.
flags.why_it_matters: Ordering the wrong size expecting free resizing can force an exchange or custom remake outside the return window.
flags.action: Confirm exact finger size before ordering and verify resizing/return eligibility in writing.

flags.label: Resizing by another jeweller voids the return or exchange right
flags.what: Ross-Simons' returns page states in capitals that items 'RESIZED BY ANOTHER JEWELLER ARE NOT ELIGIBLE FOR RETURN OR EXCHANGE', and Sarraf's returns policy likewise refuses items 'resized (by a jeweler other than Sarraf Jewelry Inc.)'. Both sellers do offer their own resizing, so the exclusion only bites if the buyer uses a third party.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the exact trap behind the brief's 'return policy — resized/custom exclusions' checklist item: a buyer who has the ring sized locally on arrival can lose the return right entirely, and the seller's own XRF or appraisal check may then have to happen on a non-returnable ring.
flags.action: Have the seller resize the ring, or confirm the return window has been used, before any third-party jeweller touches it.
flags.quote: ITEMS THAT HAVE BEEN ALTERED IN ANY WAY INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO RESIZED BY ANOTHER JEWELLER ARE NOT ELIGIBLE FOR RETURN OR EXCHANGE.

flags.label: Excessive-returns 'three strike' policy counts returns over $10,000
flags.what: Sarraf's returns policy publishes a 'NOTICE OF EXCESSIVE RETURNS': high-risk behaviour is defined as 'Returning 30 or more items', 'Returning purchases greater than $10K' or an 'Overall return rate of 85%'. Clients who reach three strikes 'will be prohibited from making any new orders'. Strikes are not assessed when the fault is Sarraf's (a damaged or incorrectly listed item).
flags.why_it_matters: A buyer returning a high-value engagement ring can be counted as high-risk purely because of the item's price, and three such returns end the account. That is a real cost of exercising a return right and belongs in the seller-reputation part of the checklist.
flags.action: Treat the return right as usable but not free of consequence: return once, decisively, and ask about the policy before ordering several high-value rings to compare at home.

flags.label: Warranty repairs cost $100 or 10% of the purchase price
flags.what: Sarraf product pages state: 'In the event that your item is defective Sarraf will at its sole discretion, repair or replace the item free of charge... If you choose not to have the item repaired or replaced by Sarraf Jewelry Inc., you will be charged a warranty fee of $100.00 or 10% of the purchase price which ever amount is greater.' Sarraf's About page separately advertises a 'Lifetime Guarantee' with 'Some restrictions apply'.
flags.why_it_matters: A 'lifetime guarantee' that charges $100 or 10% of the price (whichever is greater) the moment the buyer uses their own jeweller is not free cover. On a $3,004 ring that is a $300.40 fee.
flags.action: Read the warranty clause, not the marketing label, and price the 10% into the total cost of ownership.
flags.correction_note: Updated 2026-10-23 in Pass P6 (arena/a05b3c00-gold3): the prior URL cited by Pass P3 (.../14k-white-gold-1-00-ctw-round-3-stone-diamond-engagement-ring-g-i1-3-80-gr.html) returned HTTP 404 ('Sarraf - Not Found') and was repointed to R20's live page where chunk 4 (#tab-warranty) prints the exact $100 / 10% clause verbatim.

flags.label: Two official Sarraf pages disagree about engraved rings
flags.what: Sarraf's About page says the 30-day policy covers 'any non-engraved items still in new condition ... No questions asked', while the returns policy page says 'Any ring where personal engraving was added or a special finish may be returned, exchanged, or resized where possible (with the exception of special orders); however, the $25.00 engraving fee or $50.00 finsh charges are non-refundable.' One page excludes engraved items outright; the other accepts them with non-refundable fees.
flags.why_it_matters: A buyer who engraves a ring on the strength of the returns page may be refused under the About page's narrower wording. Where two official pages conflict, the buyer should assume the stricter one applies until the seller confirms in writing.
flags.action: Get written confirmation before engraving, or do not engrave until the return window has passed.
flags.quote: Return any non-engraved items still in new condition and we'll give you a full refund within the first 30 days. No questions asked.

flags.label: Automic lead time contradicts itself on one page
flags.what: Automic Gold product pages print conflicting production times on the same page. R22 Radiant Cathedral and R25 Gemstone Flower print 'Production time is 4-8 business days' in the buy box and 'Production time is 1-2 weeks' in Shipping & Returns. R23 Coffin Ring prints 'Production time is 1 to 5 business days' in the buy box and 'This item is made to order. Production time is 1-2 weeks' in Shipping & Returns (2-3 weeks with engraving).
flags.why_it_matters: A buyer choosing between 'in 8 days' and 'in 2 weeks (5 weeks engraved)' cannot plan. When one page gives two lead times, the longer one is the safe assumption.
flags.action: Confirm the current lead time in writing before ordering, especially for an engraved or made-to-order piece.
flags.p15_reconfirmed: 2026-10-23: R23 contradiction added from chunk 4 of the official Coffin Ring page.

flags.label: Cited official source URL returns 404
flags.what: Nine product/seller/policy URLs recorded by earlier sessions returned HTTP 404 or redirected to a generic KB index when opened live on 2026-10-23: Sarraf's https://www.sarraf.com/pages/returns-and-refunds.html (404 -> /30-day-returns-and-exchange-policy/), Automic's https://www.automicgold.com/pages/return-policy (404 -> /policies/refund-policy), Brilliant Earth's https://www.brilliantearth.com/returns/ (404 -> /30-Day-Returns/), VRAI's https://www.vrai.com/pages/contact-us (404 -> /contact-us) and https://help.vrai.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000836514-What-is-your-return-policy (redirect -> /en/knowledge/what-is-your-return-policy), Local Eclectic's https://www.localeclectic.com/pages/contact-us (404 -> /pages/frequently-asked-questions), and Menē's https://mene.com/contact-us (404 -> /customer-care/en-US). In addition, WAR1 cited dead 404 sarraf.com/.../14k-white-gold-1-00-ctw-round-3-stone-diamond-engagement-ring-g-i1-3-80-gr.html and SPEC5 cited dead 404 automicgold.com/products/1-50ctw-pear-shaped-lab-grown-diamond-engagement-ring-bezel-set. All nine records were repointed to live HTTP 200 official pages on 2026-10-23.
flags.why_it_matters: The brief requires every table row to carry a working source link to an official site. A dead citation is worse than no citation: it looks like evidence but cannot be checked, and the values attributed to it become unverifiable.
flags.action: Re-fetch every cited URL before publishing, and prefer the canonical page reached from the site's own policy index over a guessed slug.

flags.label: A flat fee is deducted from your refund
flags.what: Ross-Simons deducts a USD 4.95 flat return-shipping fee from every refund, and Catbird deducts an $9 return-shipping charge. Neither fee is a restocking charge and neither is waived for a faulty item; both are printed on the seller's own returns page.
flags.why_it_matters: The refund you receive is not the price you paid. On a $249 ring a $4.95 fee is 2%; on a $276 ring a $9 fee is 3.3%. A buyer comparing 'free returns' claims across sellers needs the deduction, not the headline.
flags.action: Subtract the stated fee before comparing a seller's return terms, and check whether the fee is waived when the item is wrong or faulty.
flags.quote: Ross-Simons: 'A $4.95 flat rate will be deducted from your refund.' Catbird: 'An $9 charge for return shipping will be deducted from your refund.'

flags.label: Seller re-prices continuously - a captured price is not today's price
flags.what: Menē sells by gram weight and re-quotes as the metal price moves. Every Menē row in this project has now moved down more than once, and the movement continued on the evening of 2026-10-23: the Classic Band product page printed $1,694 (captured $1,707 earlier that day, $1,720 on 2026-10-22) and the Narrow Flat Band printed $1,532 (captured $1,544). On the same evening GoldPrice.org printed $3,997.22/oz against the $4,022.22/oz snapshot the melt values use — a 0.62% fall on the same market date. Menē's Wide Flat Band page returned HTTP 500 during that read (see SRC3).
flags.why_it_matters: A price copied from a research page is a dated observation, not a quote a seller can be held to. On a metal-linked listing the figure you pay is whatever the page prints at checkout, and any melt-value ratio computed from the older figure drifts with it.
flags.action: Open the source link and read the live price before comparing or buying. Treat every price on this site as captured on the date printed beside it, and re-check it the day you order — a Menē figure can move twice in one day.
flags.quote: Classic Band From $1,664 ... Narrow Flat Band From $1,544 ... Wide Flat Band From $2,315

flags.label: Cited contact page returned HTTP 500 (repointed to live /facts page)
flags.what: Catbird's /contact-us URL returned "HTTP 500 Internal Server Error" (nginx) across multiple checks on 2026-10-23. Session arena/15b00e99-gold3 confirmed that https://www.catbirdnyc.com/facts returns HTTP 200 and prints 'customerservice@catbirdnyc.com' verbatim, so S-CB and catbird now cite /facts while keeping this flag to warn buyers that /contact-us is failing.
flags.why_it_matters: A broken contact page impedes post-purchase support; buyers should use customerservice@catbirdnyc.com or returns.narvar.com/catbird directly.
flags.action: Contact customerservice@catbirdnyc.com (verified on catbirdnyc.com/facts) or use returns.narvar.com/catbird.
flags.quote: 500 Internal Server Error on /contact-us; customerservice@catbirdnyc.com confirmed live on /facts

flags.label: Collection card price differs materially from live product page price
flags.what: Mejuri's milestone-rings collection card (chunk 2) prints 'From $648' for Slim Diamond Eternity Band (R03), while opening the linked 14k Solid White Gold product page on the exact same pass prints 'From $898' (+38.6%). Menē's Wide Flat Band similarly prints 'From $2,315' on the collection grid vs '$2,465 USD' on the product page.
flags.why_it_matters: A collection-grid 'From' card can lag price increases or display a discontinued/smaller variant, understating checkout cost by hundreds of dollars.
flags.action: Always verify the exact variant price directly on the product page at checkout — never rely on collection-grid 'From' cards.

flags.label: Standalone refund policy contradicts product-page return shipping terms
flags.what: Wilson's Estate Jewelry's product-page Domestic Returns tab (R11–R13) states 'Returns within the US are complimentary!' via a prepaid QR label within 3 calendar days of label receipt, whereas its standalone policy page (/policies/refund-policy) omits complimentary labels and states 'You must ship the package back to us, insured for the retail value'.
flags.why_it_matters: Insured shipping on a $1,690–$7,050 ring costs $50–$150+; if the standalone refund policy controls, the buyer bears both the cost and transit risk.
flags.action: Obtain written email confirmation before checkout that the seller will issue a complimentary fully insured US return label if returned.

flags.label: Selected band style contradicts published pavé carat weight on same page
flags.what: On VRAI's Petite 4-Prong Solitaire page (R28), the active configuration reads 'Band: Plain band', yet the Setting Details block on the exact same page prints 'Pavé carat weight: 0.11ctw'.
flags.why_it_matters: Shared template specs on configurable ring pages make it unclear whether the selected plain shank is supposed to carry pavé melee, affecting the written order specification and potentially resizing. R28's price remains blank because no price was shown in the static page text; no price is asserted here.
flags.action: Confirm exact SKU specifications (plain shank vs pavé melee carat weight) on the written order invoice before paying.
flags.p15_correction: 2026-10-23: corrected the ring name from Signature 6-Prong to Petite 4-Prong, removed an unrelated $1,460 figure and repointed the source to the R28 page actually read.

flags.label: Material heading contradicts the material actually selected
flags.what: On Mejuri's Bold Diamond Eternity Ring (R01) and Slim Diamond Eternity Band (R03) the swatch line and body copy name "Solid White Gold (14k)", while the Materials & Specifications subheading on the same page prints "Solid Yellow Gold (14k)". The karat (14k) is consistent; the colour is not. Read live on 2026-10-23.
flags.why_it_matters: A buyer ordering white gold is shown a heading that says yellow gold. Both are 14k solid gold, so purity is unaffected, but the page contradicts itself and the colour should be confirmed in writing on the order.
flags.action: Ask the seller in writing to confirm the metal colour of the exact variant ordered; keep the reply with the order confirmation.

flags.label: Cross-dataset audit quarantined unverified static-HTML weights & false BBB rating on Menē
flags.what: Cross-dataset review of Menē across Dataset B (R30, S-MENE) and Dataset C (BND-01..03, SEL-MENE) caught three defects in Dataset C: (1) BND-01..03 asserted static HTML gram numbers that do not appear in Menē's HTML (gram breakdown sits behind a client-side JS modal), (2) SEL-MENE recorded a false 'D+' BBB grade (both official BBB files 0107-1413670 & 0107-1378080 are 'Not Rated'), and (3) SEL-MENE omitted Menē's 10% restocking fee and +/-0.5g (in-stock) / +/-1.0g (Crafted-on-Demand) weight tolerances.
flags.why_it_matters: Under the project's No-Hallucinations rule, no gram weight, melt value, or reputation grade may stand unless present verbatim in the static primary source.
flags.action: Record live screenshot of Menē's JS 'Price breakdown' modal at checkout, weigh the delivered ring against Menē's Certificate of Authenticity (within +/-0.5g in-stock / +/-1.0g MTO), and keep the COA intact.

flags.label: Must mail return within 14 days to avoid a restocking fee
flags.what: Automic Gold's refund policy allows returns within 30 days of delivery, but states: 'To avoid a restocking fee, please mail your items within 14 days.' Custom, modified and engraved items are final sale, and any diamond certificate must be returned with the ring.
flags.why_it_matters: While the headline window is 30 days, waiting past day 14 to mail the package exposes the buyer to an unquantified restocking fee.
flags.action: Complete independent weighing and XRF testing and drop the return package in the mail within 14 calendar days of delivery.
flags.quote: To avoid a restocking fee, please mail your items within 14 days. Items must be in their original, unworn condition.

flags.label: Cited product page returned HTTP 500 while the seller's own pages still link it
flags.what: Menē's Wide Flat Band page (https://mene.com/products/mene-wide-flat-band-gold) answered our fetch on 2026-10-23T20:31Z with “500 Internal Server Error / Page Not Found | Menē”. Menē's own Classic Band and Narrow Flat Band pages link that exact URL and print “Wide Flat Band - Gold … From $2,297”. A buyer therefore cannot confirm the band's own price on the product page at the time of reading, and the BND-03 record keeps its captured $2,465 rather than adopting the collection-level “From” figure.
flags.why_it_matters: The price you can actually transact at is the one on the product page. When that page errors, the only number visible is a “From” floor on another page, which is not the same figure and cannot be substituted without guessing.
flags.action: Re-open the link before buying; if it still errors, call Menē customer care and get the price for your size in writing, and treat BND-03's stored price as unconfirmed on the day you order.
flags.quote: 500 Internal Server Error — returned by /products/mene-wide-flat-band-gold; "Wide Flat Band - Gold ... From $2,297" read on Menē's own Recommended widget the same evening.

flags.label: Fresh gold feeds differ from the preserved calculation anchor
flags.what: P17 reopened GoldPrice.org at $3,995.88/oz and Kitco bid at $3,994.90/oz; the feeds agree within 0.0245% but sit below the preserved $4,022.22/oz calculation snapshot used by the site. The live values are published only as labelled reference readings and never consumed by melt arithmetic.
flags.why_it_matters: A re-check reading displayed as though it were the calculation anchor would silently move every melt value. The dated primary capture stays fixed until a deliberate, dated re-anchor.
flags.action: Enter the live spot quote of the purchase date into the calculator; use scripts/refresh_spot_anchor.py only with a fresh dated capture if the owner requests a re-anchor.
flags.quote: Spot Gold Price: USD 3,995.88 / Ounce | Spot Silver Price: USD 53.92 / Ounce Oct 23rd, 2026 at 07:41 NY Time

flags.label: Trustpilot totals and response rates drift between reads
flags.what: Aurate printed 4,876 reviews, Blue Nile 1,937 with replies to 97% of negative reviews, and Mejuri 5,785 with replies to 98% on the P17 live re-read. Stored counts/quotes/rates were refreshed; Ring Concierge remains an unclaimed 7-review profile and Catbird a 56-review profile with no recent invitations.
flags.why_it_matters: Review totals and solicitation practices change. A stale number or missing sample-size warning overstates confidence in seller reputation.
flags.action: Open each Trustpilot profile immediately before purchase and read the complaint themes, not just the score.

flags.label: Dataset A source links and page-text scope required precision
flags.what: P17 tightened six source links from collection pages to the exact PDPs that print the values, corrected the Ring Concierge 2.72 live clarity from E VS1 to E VVS2, and labelled Catbird’s word “Solid” as browser-title metadata rather than the visible product heading. No Dataset A price changed.
flags.why_it_matters: A broadly correct collection link or a stale note can hide a variant-specific difference. The evidence link should be the page that prints the claimed value.
flags.action: Use the exact linked PDP for each row and confirm variant, certificate and visible body text in writing before purchase.
